clue.text: One happy to include lots of US money with advance?

definitions.text: One happy to include lots of US money with advance?

indicators.note: to include means the word for happy holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: happy means merry

indicators.note: lots of means most of, so the coin's name is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: a cent is a coin of US money
A is an abbreviation for advance, as in money paid ahead

explanation.surface: A question about someone pleased to pocket a pile of dollars as an upfront payment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a hired soldier is happy so long as plenty of cash is paid up front. 'lots of' trims CENT to CEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired soldier fighting for pay is exactly someone keen on cash paid in advance.

clue.text: Joe's flaky ice cream, whipped up

parts.note: an ordinary Joe is a man

indicators.note: flaky suggests the words flake away to their first letters

explanation.surface: A man's Flake 99, the soft ice cream cone with a chocolate bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A Flake 99 is a British ice-cream cone with a chocolate flake pushed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes someone frenzied and agitated, as if worked into a lather.

clue.text: Sailors' smokes

definitions.meaning: sailors who reef the sails, and short double-breasted jackets sailors wear

explanation.surface: What seafarers puff on.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer names both a seaman who reefs sails and a joint of cannabis.

clue.text: Cream, the low-calorie drug?

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug
lite is the marketing spelling of light, meaning low in calories

explanation.surface: A dessert cream sold as a diet-friendly substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like food, but it means the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, the select few.

clue.text: Party ousting leader with resistance may set alarm bells ringing

indicators.note: ousting leader means the first letter of the party word is thrown out

parts.note: to carouse is to party drunkenly
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A party coup against its leader alarms people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics, but it is the verb carouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rouses stirs people up and wakes them, as an alarm does.

clue.text: Desires Japanese income?

parts.note: Y stands for the yen, the Japanese currency
earnings are one's income

explanation.surface: A question about wanting money earned in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearnings are strong longings, so desires.

clue.text: Card game, no limit

indicators.note: no limit says the game's name loses its final letter, its limit

parts.note: jacks is a children's game of tossing and catching small pieces

explanation.surface: A note on a card game played without any cap on stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card game' reads as one phrase, but 'Card' alone is the definition, the court card below the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is a playing card ranked between the ten and the queen.

clue.text: Attacking politician's ego restrained by psychologist

indicators.note: restrained by means the inner pieces are held inside the psychologist's name

parts.note: Carl Jung was the Swiss psychologist
MP is a Member of Parliament
I is the self, the ego

explanation.surface: An aggressive politician's self-image is held in check by a psychologist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping on someone means pouncing to attack them.

clue.text: Brando said he could have been one against money

definitions.text: Brando said he could have been one

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
tender is money, as in legal tender

explanation.surface: A film reference set against cash.
explanation.walkthrough: In On the Waterfront, Marlon Brando's character says 'I coulda been a contender'.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a rival competing for a title, as in boxing.

clue.text: Can I go hysterical about the Spanish renaissance artist?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the Spanish article
hysterical suggests wild disorder, so the letters of Can I go are jumbled

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: An excitable invitation to go and see a Spanish painter of the Renaissance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hysterical' gives ANGICO, which 'about' wraps round the article. Fra Angelico was in fact Italian; 'Spanish' serves only the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Fra Angelico was a fifteenth-century Florentine painter of the early Renaissance.

clue.text: Top politician produced pop in the '80s

indicators.note: Top says the politician's name loses its top, its first letter, in a down-the-page sense of front

parts.note: Alex Salmond was the Scottish National Party leader and First Minister of Scotland

explanation.surface: A leading politician once had a career making 1980s pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top politician' reads as a senior figure, but 'Top' removes the first letter from SALMOND. Marc Almond sang with Soft Cell in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Almond, singer of Soft Cell's Tainted Love, was an 1980s pop star.

clue.text: Edges of space probed by science project

indicators.note: probed by means the outer letters are entered by the science piece placed between them
Edges of picks the first and last letters of space

parts.note: chem is short for chemistry, a science

explanation.surface: A space exploration project where the outer reaches are explored by scientists.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a plan or undertaking, the same as a project.

clue.text: Defender playing table tennis, discarding broken bat

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of table tennis are put into play and rearranged
discarding broken says the letters of bat, scattered, are removed from the jumble

parts.note: bat is taken as written, its letters removed

explanation.surface: A ping-pong defender carries on playing after throwing away a broken bat.
explanation.walkthrough: TABLETENNIS less the letters B, A, T leaves LETENNIS, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a guard or sentry who defends a place.

clue.text: Being against rhymes on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: verses are rhymes or lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Radio poetry described as being opposed to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus is Latin for against, used as in one team playing against another.

clue.text: Special powers aren't deciphering old language

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is a special power

indicators.note: deciphering suggests the letters of aren't are puzzled into a new order

explanation.surface: Psychic abilities are no help in decoding an ancient tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old language' looks like one phrase, but Esperanto is a constructed language from the 1880s.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language.

clue.text: Struggle to penetrate compound interest? Throw in towel

indicators.note: to penetrate means the struggle word goes inside the jumbled letters
compound means the letters of interest are mixed together
Throw says the letters of in are thrown out of the jumble

parts.note: taken as written, letters removed
to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: Fighting through compound interest, a debtor finally throws in the towel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw in towel' reads as giving up, but 'Throw' discards IN from the interest letters, and 'compound' scrambles the TEREST left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviette is a table napkin, a small towel for the hands at meals.

clue.text: Wilder's comeback in comical Dear Outlaw

indicators.note: in means the reversed name sits inside the rearranged letters
comical suggests the letters of Dear are played around with
comeback means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Gene Wilder was the American comic actor

explanation.surface: A comedy film comeback by Gene Wilder titled Dear Outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Gene Wilder was the comic actor of Young Frankenstein; 'comical' gives READ, split round the reversal that 'comeback' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade is a rebel or outlaw who has deserted their side.

clue.text: Rainbow's guitar player left out

parts.note: the 's of Rainbow's is read as a letter S standing at the front

indicators.note: left out says the L, for left, is dropped from the guitar player's name

parts.note: a plectrum is the small pick used to play a guitar

explanation.surface: A guitarist from the band Rainbow has been dropped from the line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Rainbow is also a rock band, so 'guitar player' looks like a person; it is the pick. The 's of Rainbow's supplies the S that goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is the band of colours light splits into, as seen in a rainbow.

clue.text: Army officer's gone wandering in Germany

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in Germany

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: wandering suggests the letters of gone stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A colonel has gone walkabout in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne, or Koln, is a city on the Rhine in Germany.

clue.text: With MS .NET I'd hack Outlook

indicators.note: hack suggests computer code chopped about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hacking Microsoft Outlook using Microsoft's .NET software.
explanation.walkthrough: MS .NET and Outlook look like Microsoft products; Outlook is the definition in its ordinary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a person's habitual way of looking at things, their outlook.

clue.text: Confident of Home Counties treatment

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the south-east of England, SE
a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: Assurance about how things are handled in the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure can mean feeling sure and safe, untroubled by doubt.

clue.text: Australian bird, wow! Everage's finale has everyone standing

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow

indicators.note: finale picks the last letter of Everage
standing in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Dame Edna Everage's big finish wins a standing ovation from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Edna Everage was Barry Humphries's Australian comic character.
explanation.definitionFit: The corella is a white Australian cockatoo.

clue.text: Number 10 cuts Leveson's extremes after hearing rejects article

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
rejects means the article is thrown out of the court hearing

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: cuts means the figures slice between the outer letters
extremes picks the first and last letters of Leveson's

parts.note: 10 is written as the digits I and O, one and zero

explanation.surface: Downing Street trims the Leveson report's extreme proposals after a hearing turns down an article.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 Downing Street is the Prime Minister's residence; the Leveson Inquiry examined British press ethics. 'Number' looks like the address but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trillion is a very large number, a million million.

clue.text: Countless insides of pyramids are in ruins

indicators.note: in ruins means the letters are collapsed and rebuilt in a new order
insides of drops the first and last letters of pyramids

explanation.surface: An observation that the interiors of countless pyramids lie in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: PYRAMIDS less its outer letters is YRAMID, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriad as an adjective means innumerable, too many to count.

clue.text: Am I nervous? Somewhat, being underground

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone working below ground asks whether they are a bit anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner is a person, a being, who works down in a mine.

clue.text: A story on the Nostromo, initially?

definitions.text: A story on the Nostromo, initially?

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Nostromo

explanation.surface: A tale set aboard the Nostromo, the spaceship of a famous film.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nostromo is the spaceship in the 1979 film of this name; the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The film about the crew of the Nostromo is Ridley Scott's 1979 science-fiction horror.

clue.text: Consider turning over good piece

indicators.note: over means the reversed word goes over and around the letter for good
turning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to think is to consider

explanation.surface: Reflecting on a nice item while turning it over in one's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses THINK to KNIHT, which 'over' wraps round G.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight is one of the pieces in chess.

clue.text: Sir Clive, at first in trouble, accepts 50% of Sugar's backing

definitions.text: Sir Clive, at first in trouble, accepts 50% of Sugar's backing

indicators.note: accepts means the jumbled title takes the other pieces inside it
trouble suggests Sir, the initial of Clive and in are stirred up together
at first picks the first letter of Clive

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backing means the half name is read backwards

parts.note: Sugar is the businessman Alan Sugar, and half of his first name is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Sir Clive, struggling early on, accepts that Lord Sugar will back half of the business.
explanation.walkthrough: Sugar is Alan Sugar of Amstrad, which bought Sinclair's computer business in 1986. 'trouble' gives SINCIR, and 'backing' turns AL, half of ALAN, into LA for the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Clive Sinclair, inventor of the ZX Spectrum, saw his firm rescued by Amstrad's purchase.

clue.text: Wisdom's extremely likeable with heart of gold

indicators.note: with heart of puts the gold piece at the centre of the outer letters
extremely picks the first and last letters of likeable

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Wise advice that's thoroughly charming, coming from a heart of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is traditional knowledge handed down, a body of wisdom.

clue.text: Junket to occupy harbour

definitions.meaning: to junket is to feast or make merry, as when hosting guests
to occupy someone is to keep them amused
to harbour a thought is to hold it in mind

explanation.surface: A trip on the taxpayer turns into an occupation of the port.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertaining can mean feasting guests, keeping someone amused, or holding an idea in mind.
